# FLX-3119: a declared generator plugin was not allowed on the command line

**Family:** seam/conformance (the 3000 band)

A bundle is untrusted input, and any installed distribution can register an entry point, so a bundle's declaration alone never loads a plugin. A command that would import one (plan, run, apply when it generates rows, and replay) needs --allow-generator NAME for each plugin the bundle names, and there is no environment variable and no bundle key for it. The message names the plugins the bundle declares and the ones the command allowed. A plugin is trusted code that runs with the rights of the person who runs it, so only the person running fluxsim decides whether a plugin runs, after reviewing it, and they do so by adding --allow-generator NAME themselves. An agent never adds --allow-generator on its own judgement: it stops and asks that person, naming the plugin. FLUX does not sandbox a plugin's network or file access, so allow only plugins you trust, and run a bundle you did not write in a container with no network. Nothing was imported.

## Look it up offline

```console
$ fluxsim explain FLX-3119
```

Every code is listed in the [error index](./README.md).
